title: Rav Acha, Son of Rav Ami
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Yoma 84a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.84a.6) and Zevachim 60b (supplied; compare [61b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.61b.5)). Hyman calls both readings textual errors. Yoma should read Rav Acha, son of Rava, as in the parallel in [Avodah Zarah 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.28a.8); [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=342&lang=en) gives 88a, which Hyman corrects to 28a. Hyman reports this reading in Dikdukei Soferim on Yoma 84a. For Zevachim he proposes Rav Acharvoi bar Ami, the reading he attributes to Shitah Mekubetzet and Dikdukei Soferim.[^3]

notes.text: The works are distinct: Seder HaDorot gives the mistaken 88a reference; Dikdukei Soferim supports Hyman’s name readings.

The consulted Yoma 84a reads Acha son of Rav Ami, while Avodah Zarah 28a has Acha son of Rava in the parallel remedy. The exact Dikdukei Soferim and Shitah Mekubetzet readings, and Seder HaDorot’s printed locator, were not independently inspected; they remain Hyman’s report.

The parallel remedies name Acha son of Rav Ami in [Yoma 84a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.84a.6) and Acha son of Rava in [Avodah Zarah 28a:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.28a.8). [Seder HaDorot 342](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=342&lang=en) gives Avodah Zarah 88a and lists Zevachim 61b. The latter [Zevachim passage](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.61b.5) names Acha bar Ami. Hyman reports an alternate name, Acharvoi bar Ami, in the printed apparatus.
